text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)

THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW Rupert Murdoch's News Corp said yesterday it was selling its 40 per cent stake in its magazine division PMP Communications for A$325 million. The move follows market fragmentation and falling sales due to a flooding of the market, the availability of international titles and competition from other media. Page 1.

The Federal Government announced yesterday it would allow existing mobile phone carriers Telstra, Optus and Vodafone to bid for new radio frequencies to be auctioned later this year. They will be not be allowed to bid the first half, or 10 megaHertz, of the frequencies, but the decision will allow Telstra to defend its position in the mobile phone market. Page 1.

Kerry Packer's private company Conspress International NV is likely to receive almost A$550 million from the sale of stock in United States print insert company Valassis Communications Inc, after enormous demand for the shares. Conspress will sell 18 million shares for US$24, decreasing its stake in Valassis from 50.3 per cent to 5.4 per cent. Page 19.

Stockbroker J.B. Were has announced an issue of A$210 million in exchangeable notes based on stock in the Foster's Brewing Group. The move follows the broker's recent placement of BHP's 31 percent stake in Foster's and News Corporation's sale of its stake in PMP Communications. Page 19.

The Coles Myer Ltd board announced yesterday that executive director Peter Morgan would leave the board following the retirement of independent chairman Nobby Clark. New chairman Stan Wallis said Morgan resigned in order to maintain "an appropriate ratio of independent to non-independent directors". Page 21.

Fletcher Challenge Ltd chief executive-designate Michael Andrews, currently head of the energy and forestry divisions, said yesterday Fletcher was unlikely to change its present structure of four separately traded divisions in the near future. Andrews will take control of the company on 14 December when current chief executive Hugh Fletcher retires. Page 20.
THE AUSTRALIAN

In the second part of an Australian Tax Office strategy on the trade in franking credits, information from the Australian Stock Exchange on security loans dating back to 1 July 1995 will be used to assess the viability of launching test cases to challenge franking credit claims. Page 23.

Amcor's printing and writing papers unit Australian Paper alleged yesterday that paper manufacturers in 14 countries were illegally dumping high-quality coated paper into the Australian market. Amcor's action claims it is caught in an international paper war that threatens its A$380 million domestic strategy and 5,000 jobs. Page 23.

Standard and Poors gave Arnotts a AA- rating yesterday for its first move into the corporate debt market, a A$100 million fixed note issue. The rating is the highest given to a corporate debt issue outside the Government and banking sectors and is likely to raise the profile of the corporate debt market. Page 23.

News Corporation Ltd yesterday confirmed it has sold its 40 percent stake in magazine publisher PMP Communications for A$325 million in a bid to raise funds through the sale of non-core assets. The 101.57 million PMP shares were believed to have been placed with a range of investors at A$3.20 a share by stockbroker JB Were & Son at a greatly reduced amount to PMP's pre-sale trading price. Page 25.

An industry coalition has told the Federal Government that the relaxation of dumping law legislation concerning China would be catastrophic for jobs and investment. The group - which includes the MTIA, ICI and Pacific Brands - also criticised the Government for going back on a promise to protect Australian business interests and of having a closed mind to industry concerns. Page 25.

Energy Resources of Australia is relying on the support of local Aboriginal groups to avoid a budget blowout at its Northern Territory Jabiluka uranium project. The mine needs the Gundjehmi community's approval for the construction of a haulage road to link the Jabiluka with the nearby Ranger uranium mine. Page 25.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Investor Paul Ramsay is looking to benefit from the private healthcare boom by raising A$80 million for a partial public float which will value Ramsay Health Care's Australian arm at A$200 million. The plan by investment banker County NatWest would see Ramsay's 100 percent stake reduced to 60 percent after the issuing of new shares. Page 29.

Yesterday's move by News Corp to sell its A$325 million controlling stake in magazine group PMP Communications could see Melbourne establishment stockbroker JB Were holding between 20 and 30 percent of the PMP company. Last night Were was still looking to find buyers for a large amount of the 101.5 million PMP shares bought from News Corp at A$3.20 each. Page 29.

A strong demand from private clients and local fund managers may secure Imperial Chemical Industries a top price for its ICI Australia shares. The chance of the price being in the top range of expectations at A$12.80 has increased after local institutions bid for three times the number of shares they were allocated. Page 29.

An OECD survey has found Australian manufacturing has the worst level of productivity among the 12 leading industrialised countries studied, and despite a number of tariff reductions and other efficiency reforms the nation has lost ground since 1960. After analysing the OECD study, Australian forecasting firm Access Economics described local manufacturing productivity levels as "appalling" and "depressing". Page 29.

Discussions over how the Seven Network and the Australian Broadcasting Corporation will collaborate on the ABC's Australia Television Asian satellite service has led to speculation that Seven will be the successful bidder for the service. The ABC was ordered to sell the loss-making venture last year by the Federal Government after it was revealed Australia Television was unlikely to gain sufficient advertising revenue in the short-term to become self-funding. Page 31.

Financial industry groups have criticised renewed Real Estate Institute of Australia calls to make some superannuation available to first-home-buying low-income earners. The Life Insurance and Superannuation Association and the Financial Planning Association claim there is a risk such a plan would disadvantage Australians in the long term. Page 31.
THE AGE

Increased competition in the Victorian electricity market as independent retailers battle distributors for market share has seen some customers receive discounts of up to 40 per cent. Six large Melbourne and Sydney consumers claim they have achieved discounts of at least 30 percent by tendering out their electricity supply, saving some companies millions of dollars annually. Page B1.

Australian Prime Minister John Howard has defended the sale of two-thirds of the nation's gold reserves, claiming miners themselves were partly responsible for the drop in gold prices. Despite the Federal Government and the Reserve Bank being criticised by the industry, unionists and State politicians, Howard said the sale was a "shrewd, correct, defensible investment decision". Page B1.

The decision by News Corporation to sell its A$325 million controlling stake in the PMP Communications magazine group could see Melbourne establishment stockbroker J.B. Were holding between 20 and 30 per cent of the communications company. Were managing director Terry Campbell said the offer is open for another 48 hours. Page B1.

The Federal Government is to sell key parts of the Australian radio spectrum later this year using an auction system that favours the entry of new players into the rapidly expanding mobile telephone market. The auction could result in a windfall of A$1 billion in earnings for the Government. Page B3.

Investor Paul Ramsay is looking to take advantage of the private healthcare boom by raising A$80 million for a partial public float which valuing Ramsay Health Care's Australian operation at A$200 million. Ramsay Health Care's earnings before interest and tax law year was A$20.6 million. Page B3.

An unusual debt security measure that commits J.B. Were Capital Markets to delivering investors 70 million Foster's Brewing Group shares will see Were raise A$210 million. The group is to issue 70 million notes at A$3 each to raise A$210 million capital for J.B. Were Capital Markets' future needs. Page B3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
